tagline: Virginia's road to the Ohio, over Laurel and Cheat.
intro: The designated byway is US 50 across Taylor and Preston counties, and the road drawn here picks it up early, at Bridgeport. US 50 keeps to the line of the old Northwestern Turnpike through Pruntytown and the railroad town of Grafton, then climbs over Laurel and Cheat mountains toward the Maryland line. On the Cheat the grade runs three miles at 9 percent, with 28 curves.

Virginia's 1827 plan ran it through important towns and into country the engineers could not get through, so the road was laid out again. Its chief engineer, Claudius Crozet, had served in Napoleon's artillery in Russia. The small towns along it grew on the turnpike's trade and on the B&O line beside it.
season: The West Virginia Byways and Backways guide says the valleys can be enjoyed at any time of year but are arguably at their best in summer and fall.

moments.title: Pruntytown
moments.text: An 1835 gazetteer found this crossroads with 18 houses, one tavern, one tanyard, a hatter, a tailor and a gun smith, and 110 people in all.

moments.title: Grafton
moments.text: Andrews Methodist Episcopal Church downtown held the first official Mother's Day celebration in 1908, on the Sunday Anna Jarvis chose because it marked the anniversary of her mother's death.

moments.title: Cathedral State Park
moments.text: Just east of Aurora, a town named for its altitude, trees up to 90 feet tall, most of them hemlock, stand in the largest tract of virgin timber left in West Virginia.
